title: Transactions More Than 3 Standard Deviations Above Mean
description: Detect **extreme outlier transactions** by finding those with a z-score greater than 3 standard deviations above the **global mean** across all transactions. Show the transaction, z-score, and global statistics.
solution_sql: SELECT t.transaction_id, t.account_id, t.amount, ROUND(global_stats.mean_amount, 2) AS global_mean, ROUND(global_stats.std_amount, 2) AS global_std, ROUND((t.amount - global_stats.mean_amount) / NULLIF(global_stats.std_amount, 0), 2) AS z_score FROM transactions t CROSS JOIN (SELECT AVG(amount) AS mean_amount, STDDEV(amount) AS std_amount FROM transactions) global_stats WHERE (t.amount - global_stats.mean_amount) / NULLIF(global_stats.std_amount, 0) > 3 ORDER BY z_score DESC

test_cases.description: 1 extreme outlier: transaction_id=16, amount=9500.00 with z-score > 3 against 15 normal transactions clustered around $100.

hints: Compute global AVG and STDDEV in a subquery and CROSS JOIN it to the transactions table — this attaches global statistics to every row without grouping.
Z-score = (amount - mean) / std; filter WHERE z_score > 3. Use NULLIF(std, 0) to avoid division by zero if all values are identical.
explanation: The CROSS JOIN broadcasts global statistics (mean≈688, std≈2350 due to the outlier) to every row. The outlier transaction of $9500 on Jan 16 has z = (9500 - 688) / 2350 ≈ 3.75 > 3. The 15 normal transactions around $100 each have z ≈ (100 - 688) / 2350 ≈ -0.25 — well below the threshold. This global approach is simpler than per-account z-scores and effective for detecting egregious outliers.
